What we call a “chance meeting” is usually the result of lots of causal factors: our routines and routes (traffic patterns, where we spend time), social networks and shared activities (network theory and sociology), split-second attention and memory processes in the brain (neuroscience), and instincts/chemistry that guide attraction (hormones, psychology). Those factors make certain meetings more probable than others, even if the exact moment looks random. Science doesn’t have to take away meaning — it just gives mechanisms and probabilities. That said, there are limits to current knowledge and room for faith or purpose alongside scientific explanation.
